correctness.rationale: For each starting trajectory the final position is i+A+B_i mod n; synchronization makes all B_i residues distinct, so some trajectory has at least n-1 b-events. Each gap between such events has at least n-1 a letters, forcing W as subsequence. W directly resets by the shrinking interval S_j. All next-length words are one-letter insertions; the t<j, t=j, t>j interval analysis accounts for every b insertion, while internal a insertion loses a compression. The count n^2-4n+7 covers n=2 separately. Two standalone programs verify n=2..12 by exhaustive word dynamic programming and n=2..30 by direct insertion simulation, without replacing the proof.

value.rationale: The standard Cerny family is an extremal calibration example in synchronization. Unlike simply reproducing the known shortest length, a forbidden-subsequence theorem constrains every reset protocol and gives an exact coefficient of the first excess-length layer of its reset language. The polynomial count quantifies the number of one-symbol slack choices and the precise unsafe insertion sites, providing a natural word-language invariant for comparing redundancy/rigidity of near-minimal reset sequences; the exact quantity is neither arbitrary parameter slicing nor immediate from the classical optimum.
